subject: Clarify ledger transaction samples and EU VAT responsibility
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@greenbyte.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: finance@greenbyte.com
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2027 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Unexpected ledger entries in Nov — sample txns attached

Hi Neha,

We're reconciling November and noticed ~18k tokens that don't map to any session id in our internal logs. The charges appear under two different entity tags in the export (entity:GB-EU and entity:GB-US). Can you please confirm which entity Redwood assigned to those request lines and whether VAT was applied to them as EU-supplied services?

I've attached a short sample (greenbyte_sample_txns.csv) with three transaction IDs and timestamps; the charges are small individually but aggregate to a noticeable overage on our month-end. Also attaching the invoice for reference.

Questions we have:
- Can you map the three sample txn IDs to your internal request IDs and the routing entity?
- If routing mismatched between entities, can this trigger EU VAT treatment differences?
- We requested a usage-export last week (HS-542198) — did that complete with entity tags?

We need this for our tax team; if VAT exposure is different than billed, we may need a corrected invoice or credit. Happy to jump on a 20-min call if easier.

Thanks,
Olivia Park
Finance Manager, GreenByte
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@greenbyte.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2027 13:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected ledger entries in Nov — sample txns attached

Hi Olivia — thanks for the sample and the invoice. I pulled the three transaction IDs you sent and attached the matching rows from our request log (redwood_usage_export_Q4.csv) for your review. Quick summary up front:

- The three sample txns you highlighted were routed to a pooled gateway that we use for burst routing; the pooled gateway is correctly attributed to GB-EU, but two of the three requests used a deprecated tenant tag that did not propagate the entity override on our side — so the lines were written under GB-US in the metering ledger.
- That ledger mismatch is a tagging problem (tenant metadata not present), not a tokenization difference. We will not reclassify token counts themselves.
- VAT treatment: because the metering ledger shows GB-US for those two lines, our invoicing engine treated them as non-EU-supplied in the original run. If you expect EU VAT to apply, we can reclassify the lines and issue a corrected invoice/credit for the VAT difference after agreement.

Action items I propose:
1) Internal root cause: Ben will pull the gateway routing history and flag why the tenant tag didn't propagate.
2) Reconciliation: we'll prepare a provisional journal adjustment showing the reclassified lines and VAT delta.
3) Evidence: we'll provide a redacted request trace (request ids/time offsets) to your tax team, plus a signed correction if needed.

Next steps: Ben — can you confirm whether the tenant-tag propagation bug impacted any other customers between 2027-11-23 and 2027-11-30? Grace — once Ben confirms scope, I'll prepare the provisional credit and a short note for Olivia's tax team. Olivia — if you want to avoid a formal invoice correction right away, we can provisionally apply a credit in January while we complete the audit.

Attachments: redwood_usage_export_Q4.csv (selected rows)

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Quick internal summary:
- I pulled the gateway debug logs for the three txns. Two requests hit a routing path with an older tag-mapping table (version v2027-10-01) that had a bug: tenant_tag was not forwarded when fallback to the pooled gateway occurred. The third request was routed through the normal path and correctly preserved GB-EU.
- I don't see evidence this was a token-counting error; tokenization metadata (model, prompt_len, completion_len) matches the rows in your CSV.
- Impact window looks limited to 2027-11-23T03:00:00Z -> 2027-11-30T11:30:00Z for requests routed via that pooled gateway. I'm running a quick grep now for other customers that used the same gateway; early result: 3 other accounts had at least one routed request in that window.

I'll assemble a CSV with full matched request IDs and redacted user data (usage_report_Q4.csv) and drop it in the Drive folder Neha linked. Provisional approach I recommend:
- Prepare a VAT reclassification for the affected lines and issue a credit for the VAT delta (we'll flag it as provisional until Olivia confirms).
- Add a compensating journal if GreenByte prefers a corrected invoice instead of a credit.

Putting the CSV in Drive now: https://docs.redwood.ai/drive/GreenByte/usage-reconciliation (greenbyte_sample_txns.csv + usage_report_Q4.csv).
